$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Amazon Bedrock (runtime playground, knowledge bases, agents, AgentCore). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

bedrock.runtime.title: Bedrock Runtime playground (InvokeModel / Converse, streaming)
limitations: Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer. Converse/ConverseStream and Claude InvokeModel support function tool use and json_schema structured output (small-model reliability); InvokeModelWithResponseStream streams the model family's own events incrementally (Claude, Nova, Titan, Llama, Mistral). Converse/Claude `document` blocks (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, HTML, Markdown, text) are really parsed and the extracted text is sent to the model (legacy .doc/.xls and scanned PDFs are rejected; s3Location sources are not supported). `image` blocks (Converse, ConverseStream, Claude InvokeModel; also Vertex inlineData and Azure image_url data URLs) are answered by a small open vision model (SmolVLM-500M behind llama.cpp, Apache-2.0) when the Mesh vision pack is running, and rejected with a ValidationException otherwise (Nano never serves one; remote image URLs are never fetched). It reads clean screenshots and scans, not dense layouts or handwriting, and the model is listed (IMAGE input) only while it is served. cachePoint / cache_control checkpoints are accepted and reported as cacheRead/WriteInputTokens from a real in-process prefix cache (SHA-256 of the prompt prefix, 5-minute TTL, 1024-token minimum; Converse, ConverseStream and Claude InvokeModel) - it is accounting, the compute saving comes only from llama.cpp's own prompt cache. Reasoning: on Mesh with the reasoning pack running (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, MIT), Converse/ConverseStream additionalModelRequestFields thinking{type:enabled,budget_tokens>=1024} or reasoning_config{type:enabled} and Claude InvokeModel `thinking` return real reasoningContent (reasoningText) / thinking blocks streamed before the answer, and assistant reasoningContent from earlier turns is accepted and dropped; budget_tokens is validated but advisory (a 1.5B distill can think past it and run out of maxTokens), there is no signature or redacted content, InvokeModelWithResponseStream of non-Claude families drops the thought, and without the pack a reasoning request is a ValidationException. The 1.5B distill is for arithmetic and short logic, not a stand-in for Claude or Nova reasoning.

Nano: there is no model until the page registers one. The Bedrock overview offers 'Enable in-browser model (WebLLM)' (needs WebGPU; loads @mlc-ai/web-llm from a CDN and downloads a small model); without it every model call returns ModelNotReadyException. The in-browser model serves the console page that loaded it, not the external SDK relay endpoint.

bedrock.knowledge-bases.title: Knowledge bases (S3 data sources, ingestion, Retrieve, RetrieveAndGenerate)
limitations: Ingestion really reads the S3 data source, chunks (fixed size / hierarchical parent-child / semantic embedding-breakpoint / none) and embeds with the local embedding seam; Retrieve is exact cosine kNN (no ANN index) with overrideSearchType HYBRID (BM25 via SQLite FTS5 fused with the vector ranking by reciprocal rank fusion, the default) or SEMANTIC (vector only; scores are cosine similarities) and the full RetrievalFilter set (equals, notEquals, greaterThan/OrEquals, lessThan/OrEquals, in, notIn, startsWith, stringContains, listContains, andAll, orAll, validated like Bedrock: one operator per filter, 2-5 members, typed values), plus implicitFilterConfiguration (the small local model derives the filter from the question; invented attributes are ignored). Reranking works on Retrieve (rerankingConfiguration, metadataConfiguration) and the bedrock-agent-runtime Rerank API (amazon.rerank-v1:0 and cohere.rerank-v3-5:0 ARNs, TEXT documents only, 1000 sources, numberOfResults): by default the reranker is NOT a cross-encoder but embedding similarity blended with query-term coverage (the response trace says 'embedding+lexical'); set VYOMI_RERANK_ENDPOINT to a Jina/Cohere/llama.cpp-style /v1/rerank server (for example llama-server --reranking with a bge-reranker GGUF) to get a real cross-encoder on the Mesh; none is shipped, and Nano always uses the embedding blend. Text, CSV, HTML, Markdown, PDF (pure-Python pypdf; scanned PDFs have no OCR), DOCX, XLSX and PPTX are parsed (legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt fail); parsingStrategy BEDROCK_FOUNDATION_MODEL keeps tables as markdown but is not a model call, BEDROCK_DATA_AUTOMATION is rejected; .metadata.json sidecars (plain and typed) feed Retrieve filters; unreadable documents are listed per file in the ingestion job's failureReasons. On Nano PDF needs pypdf to be loaded into Pyodide (otherwise PDFs fail with an explicit reason). The vector store type named at creation is recorded but the index always lives in the account (no OpenSearch/Pinecone/etc). Without an embedding model on the backend, vyomi-hash-embed (a deterministic bag-of-words embedding) is used, so retrieval is lexical-ish, not semantic. Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer.

bedrock.agents.title: Agents (create, prepare, aliases, knowledge bases, InvokeAgent)
limitations: Agent versions/aliases snapshot the prepared agent; InvokeAgent prompts the local model with the instruction, session history and retrieved knowledge-base passages and returns citations. Function-schema and OpenAPI (JSON, or YAML when PyYAML is available; inline or read from S3) action groups with a Lambda executor are really invoked through the Lambda engine with the Bedrock Agents event, and the result is fed back to the model; RETURN_CONTROL groups return the returnControl event and accept returnControlInvocationResults on the next InvokeAgent. requireConfirmation (function schema, or x-requireConfirmation in OpenAPI) returns a returnControl with actionInvocationType CONFIRM; the Lambda only runs after the caller answers confirmationState CONFIRM (DENY tells the model it was refused). Built-in AMAZON.UserInput returns the model's question as the reply and the next InvokeAgent continues the session; built-in AMAZON.CodeInterpreter really runs the model's Python (Mesh/appliance: a restricted subprocess with rlimits, a wall-clock kill and an audit hook that denies sockets, process creation and file access outside a throw-away directory; Nano: an AST-gated in-process exec limited to a stdlib allow-list with a time guard and no numpy/pandas) with input files via sessionState.files (BYTE_CONTENT or S3, useCase CODE_INTERPRETER) and written files returned as a files event - it is a restricted-execution sandbox, not a VM (no network namespace, a single C call cannot be interrupted on Nano, variables do not persist between calls, no image/plot outputs unless the host Python has matplotlib, which is not verified). Multi-agent collaboration: agentCollaboration SUPERVISOR / SUPERVISOR_ROUTER with Associate/Get/List/Update/DisassociateAgentCollaborator (collaborators are deployed agent aliases, cycles rejected, depth 3); the supervisor gets one tool per collaborator and collaborator traces are relayed with collaboratorName and callerChain; SUPERVISOR_ROUTER adds a model-based routing classifier that can hand a whole request to one collaborator (routingClassifierTrace) - sequential, no parallel collaborator calls. Custom prompts: promptOverrideConfiguration (validated) overrides ORCHESTRATION (template placeholders, inferenceConfiguration), PRE_PROCESSING, POST_PROCESSING, MEMORY_SUMMARIZATION and ROUTING_CLASSIFIER, and a parser Lambda (overrideLambda, the real OUTPUT_PARSER event) can parse PRE/ORCHESTRATION (FINISH, ASK_USER, ACTION_GROUP)/POST output; KNOWLEDGE_BASE_RESPONSE_GENERATION is applied when its prompt is OVERRIDDEN and ENABLED: after each knowledge-base lookup the agent's own template ($query$, $search_results$, $output_format_instructions$) is run on the model with the prompt's inferenceConfiguration (traced as an orchestrationTrace modelInvocationInput of type KNOWLEDGE_BASE_RESPONSE_GENERATION), a parser Lambda may rewrite it (knowledgeBaseResponseGenerationParsedResponse.generatedResponse.generatedResponseParts), and the generated answer, not the raw passages, is given to orchestration (DISABLED or default: passages go to the model directly, as before); a parser returning a KNOWLEDGE_BASE invocation is rejected. InvokeInlineAgent (POST /agents/{sessionId}) runs the same loop from the request's instruction, action groups (incl. the built-ins), knowledge bases, guardrail, prompts and collaboratorConfigurations; inline collaborators (nested inline agents) and memory are not supported. Tool selection uses schema-constrained JSON output, validated against the action schema with bounded retries (after which the agent answers it is unable to assist, with a failureTrace) - a <1 GB model still chooses tools far less reliably than a production model. enableTrace emits preProcessing/orchestration/postProcessing/guardrail/failure/routingClassifier trace parts from the real loop (pre/post-processing are deterministic steps unless overridden). guardrailConfiguration applies the guardrails engine to input and output; memoryConfiguration SESSION_SUMMARY summarises a session at endSession (memoryId) and when the session idles past idleSessionTTLInSeconds (evaluated lazily on the next request that touches the agent or GetAgentMemory, there is no background clock), and feeds it to later sessions, with GetAgentMemory/DeleteAgentMemory. Not implemented: enhanced (non-text) chat inputs (sessionState.files with useCase CHAT are rejected). Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer.

bedrock.agentcore.gateway.title: AgentCore gateways and targets (MCP)
limitations: Gateways expose a real MCP JSON-RPC endpoint (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) at POST /gateways/{id}/mcp on the Vyomi wire, not at the *.gateway.bedrock-agentcore hostname. Lambda targets are really invoked. CUSTOM_JWT is really validated (RS256 signature against the JWKS of the discoveryUrl issuer - this simulator's Cognito pools in-process, any other issuer by OIDC discovery - plus issuer, expiry, allowedAudience, allowedClients, allowedScopes; 401 for bad/missing/expired tokens, 403 for audience/client/scope mismatch; RS256 only, needs `cryptography`, so it fails closed where that is unavailable). openApiSchema targets (JSON or YAML) become callable tools named <target>___<operationId> (path/query/header params and JSON body, $ref resolved) and mcpServer targets are proxied over MCP streamable HTTP; outbound calls (openApi, mcpServer, OAuth token exchange, JWKS/OIDC discovery of non-local issuers) go straight out from the Mesh/appliance; on Nano they go through the allow-listed egress relay (the hosted relay serves public https origins on its allow-list, the local tunnel serves origins mapped with `vyomi-tunnel gateway-backend`) and return an isError result with the reason when no relay is reachable. API-key and OAuth2 client-credentials credential providers (CreateApiKeyCredentialProvider / CreateOauth2CredentialProvider, GetResourceApiKey / GetResourceOauth2Token M2M) feed the target's outbound auth; the OAuth USER_FEDERATION flow (three-legged: GetResourceOauth2Token returns an authorizationUrl with PKCE S256 + state and a sessionUri, the provider's callbackUrl on this service exchanges the code with the code_verifier, CompleteResourceTokenAuth binds the session to the user, then the same call returns the access token, cached per provider/user/scopes; forceAuthentication restarts it) works against any OIDC provider with an authorization_endpoint, and against this simulator's own Cognito user pools through their hosted-UI endpoints (/{poolId}/oauth2/authorize, /login, /oauth2/token: authorization-code + PKCE on moto, Mesh/appliance only); workload access tokens (GetWorkloadAccessToken / ForUserId / ForJWT) are Vyomi-minted opaque tokens that are not signature-verified; vendor-specific discovery and ON_BEHALF_OF_TOKEN_EXCHANGE are not implemented. smithyModel targets (Smithy JSON AST, inline or from S3; awsJson1_0, awsJson1_1 and restJson1 models) are callable: every operation is a tool that runs against this simulator's own API for that service (awsQuery / ec2Query / rpcv2 models are refused at create). AWS_IAM gateways verify the SigV4 signature of an access key held by this simulator's IAM (wrong secret or an expired x-amz-date -> 403); a key IAM holds is always verified (no flag); an access key IAM does not hold (ambient dev credentials such as test/test) cannot be verified and is admitted as unverified unless VYOMI_AGENTCORE_SIGV4_STRICT=1; IAM policy evaluation (bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway) is not done, and a request signed for a different Host than the one the simulator sees (some relays) fails verification.

bedrock.agentcore.runtime.title: AgentCore runtime (hosted agents) - Vyomi agent spec, Dev Simplified
limitations: Dev Simplified: runtimes are control-plane records (CreateAgentRuntime/Get/List/Update/Delete, versions, runtime endpoints with DEFAULT, CREATING->READY) and InvokeAgentRuntime really runs an agent - but NOT your container. A runtime whose environmentVariables carry VYOMI_AGENT_SPEC (JSON: instructions + declarative tools: static/template/builtin calculator/webhook/in-process function) is executed in-process as a tool-calling loop over the local model (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano; payload {"prompt": ...}, runtimeSessionId keeps multi-turn history, Accept: text/event-stream streams token events as the model produces them, then tool_use / tool_result steps and a final event; on Nano the in-browser wire delivers the body whole). A container-only runtime returns RuntimeClientError (424); no model running -> 503 ServiceUnavailableException, never a canned answer. Quality is toy-grade; no container/ECR pull. InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand streams contentStart / contentDelta (stdout, stderr) / contentStop from the code sandbox in a per-session workspace, but it is a documented subset of sh (; && ||, > >>, echo pwd ls cat env printenv whoami uname which true false exit, python3 -c / script.py; no pipes, globs, variables, pip, npm, git or a real shell), and output arrives per command, not mid-process. Runtimes with protocolConfiguration.serverProtocol MCP (spec tools served as an MCP server: initialize, tools/list, tools/call) or A2A (JSON-RPC message/send, tasks/get, agent card; agent runs the spec over the local model) answer JSON-RPC payloads; the A2A card is also served at GET /runtimes/{arn}/invocations/.well-known/agent-card.json, and A2A message/stream answers Server-Sent task events (task, status-update, artifact-update, final status-update; one artifact-update per model token chunk as it is produced, a working status-update naming the tools after a tool-calling step, then the final artifact and completed status; on Nano the body is delivered whole); there is no push notification. AgentCore Memory (events + long-term records) is hooked in through the spec's memory block; Identity covers API-key / OAuth2 credential providers only, and a runtime created with a customJWTAuthorizer verifies inbound JWTs (RS256 signature, expiry, issuer, allowedAudience / allowedClients / allowedScopes; 401 / 403) on invocations and the agent card; runtimes without an authorizer are not authenticated. Webhook tools reach the network directly on the Mesh/appliance and through the allow-listed egress relay on Nano (a tool error with the reason when none is reachable); on Nano the loop re-runs after each model or network await, so keep tools idempotent. State is in the persisted account bag.

bedrock.guardrails.title: Guardrails (CreateGuardrail, versions, ApplyGuardrail, Converse guardrailConfig) - Dev Simplified
limitations: Dev Simplified: deterministic simple filters, not Bedrock's trained classifiers. Word lists (custom + small PROFANITY list), denied topics (name/example phrase match), regex PII (EMAIL, PHONE, US SSN, card, IP, AWS key, URL and more) with BLOCK/ANONYMIZE, custom regexes, and content filters (HATE, INSULTS, SEXUAL, VIOLENCE, MISCONDUCT, PROMPT_ATTACK) whose LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH strength is honoured against a confidence from keyword hits plus, only when a real embedding model is up, a zero-shot embedding-prototype score (conservative thresholds, not calibrated against a labelled set; without a real embedder it is keywords only). Contextual GROUNDING and RELEVANCE filters (thresholds, scores, grounding_source/query/guard_content qualifiers, Converse guardContent) are scored by word coverage plus embedding cosine: a deterministic scorer, thresholds behave the same but absolute scores differ from Bedrock's. Converse, ConverseStream, InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream check input and output; stream output is judged in ~1000-character windows (sync holds a window until judged and can mask or replace it, async streams then only reports), so a violation split across two windows can be missed. Automated reasoning, image content and cross-Region config are rejected. State is kept in the persisted space account bag and survives a restart.

bedrock.data-automation.title: Data Automation (blueprints, projects, InvokeDataAutomationAsync / InvokeDataAutomation) - small open models
limitations: Dev Simplified: real wire shapes (bedrock-data-automation + runtime) with blueprint/project/job records in the account bag and S3 in/out (job_metadata.json, standard_output/0/result.json, custom_output/0/result.json). Text-layer documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, HTML, Markdown, TXT) are parsed without a model; images (png/jpeg/gif/webp) are read by a small open vision model (SmolVLM-500M via llama.cpp, Mesh only) for OCR text and a one-line summary; blueprint (custom) output is one JSON-schema-constrained model call per blueprint (typed values or null; with several blueprints a model call picks the class). Every result.json carries a `vyomi` block naming the engine and saying so.

Quality is that of a 0.5B vision / 3B chat model, not the managed service: no confidence scores, bounding boxes, layout elements, tables or per-page geometry; scanned PDFs have no OCR (no rasteriser) and fail with a ClientError; audio and video are rejected; images need Mesh (Nano has no vision model) and custom output on Nano is declared unsupported (WebLLM cannot run in a background job). Libraries, blueprint optimisation, CopyBlueprintStage, EventBridge notifications, KMS and PII settings are not executed (libraries/optimisation return a ValidationException).

bedrock.flows.title: Flows (CreateFlow, PrepareFlow, versions, aliases, InvokeFlow with tracing) - Dev Simplified
limitations: Node types executed: Input, Output, InlineCode (Python_3 on the code sandbox: node inputs are variables, the last expression is the output; stdlib-only on Nano, no network or processes), Prompt (inline or a Prompt Management ARN), Condition (string ==, !=, contains; numeric > < >= <=; and / or; default), Iterator + Collector (per-item fan-out and an ordered join), Agent (InvokeAgent on an agent alias), KnowledgeBase (Retrieve, or RetrieveAndGenerate when a modelId is set), LambdaFunction (real invoke, needs the Lambda engine), Retrieval and Storage (S3 get/put), and Loop (LoopInput + LoopController body repeated until the controller condition is false or maxIterations). Lex nodes are rejected (Vyomi has no Lex NLU runtime to recognise an intent), as are cycles outside a Loop body. InvokeFlow with enableTrace returns flowTraceEvent nodeInputTrace / nodeOutputTrace / conditionNodeResultTrace per node execution; there is no flowMultiTurnInputRequestEvent, performance configuration or guardrail on prompt nodes. The Loop node follows the documented LoopInput / LoopController shape but is Vyomi's reading of it: the controller's `input` is fed back into LoopInput and its condition is evaluated with the same expression language as Condition nodes. Prompt, Agent and KnowledgeBase answers come from the single small local model, so flow outputs are toy-grade. A node execution cap of 1000 applies per invoke. Nano replays an InvokeFlow request around each async model call, so Lambda and Storage results are memoised during a request; the Lambda engine and outbound S3 behave as on the Mesh. The visual canvas is the console's own React Flow editor (positions are stored in the browser, not in the flow definition).

bedrock.evaluations.title: Model and RAG evaluations (CreateEvaluationJob: automatic, LLM-as-a-judge, RAG, human) - Dev Simplified
limitations: Model evaluation scores with simple open scorers (token F1 Accuracy, ROUGE-L, exact match, embedding cosine, perturbation Robustness, guardrail-lexicon Toxicity) and with LLM-as-a-judge: the judge is the single small local model, prompted per metric (Correctness, Completeness, Helpfulness, Coherence, Relevance, FollowingInstructions, ProfessionalStyleAndTone, Harmfulness, Stereotyping, Refusal, custom metrics with your own rating scale) and answering one option of a labelled rating scale that maps to 0..1. A 3B judge is far less reliable than the managed judge models: unparsable verdicts are counted as unscored records, never scored, and Harmfulness / Stereotyping / Refusal are lower-is-better. RAG evaluations run over a knowledge base: retrieve-only (ContextRelevance, ContextCoverage) and retrieve-and-generate (Correctness, Completeness, Helpfulness, LogicalCoherence, Faithfulness, CitationCoverage, CitationPrecision, Harmfulness, Stereotyping, Refusal), plus precomputed (bring-your-own) RAG output. Datasets accept the flat prompt/referenceResponse/category lines and the conversationTurns format, up to 1000 records; jobs run in batches (a background worker on the Mesh, advanced one batch per GetEvaluationJob on Nano) with progress reported while InProgress, so a job over many records finishes only as fast as the local model answers. Not the managed BERTScore or real-world-knowledge scorers. The human-workflow job type records the job and generates the model responses to S3 but the SageMaker Ground Truth work team and rating UI are not simulated: it stays InProgress awaiting reviewers until stopped, and no ratings are fabricated. Bring-your-own inference responses for model evaluation (precomputedInferenceSource) and EXTERNAL_SOURCES RAG are not supported.

bedrock.imported-models.title: Custom model import (imported models, import jobs, InvokeModel / Converse on the imported ARN)
limitations: Vyomi extension: real Bedrock imports Hugging Face weights, here s3DataSource.s3Uri is a prefix holding a LoRA adapter GGUF (adapter.gguf, up to 50 MB) and adapter_meta.json trained on Mesh or your machine. The import job validates the GGUF header, rank, hidden size and base and fails with the reason (failureMessage). The model is a SmolLM2 135M or 360M base plus your adapter, so it is a small open model, not a vendor model. Serving needs the Nano console tab (llama.cpp WASM, the base GGUF is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use, one imported model resident at a time, answers are returned whole); Mesh and offline accept and store imports but cannot serve them yet and answer ModelNotReadyException.
